name: Apollo 12
short_status: Second crewed Moon landing. Intrepid touched down 19 Nov 1969 in Oceanus Procellarum, about 160 m (535 ft) from the Surveyor 3 probe. Crew returned 24 Nov 1969. Success.
tagline: NASA · United States · Crewed landing · 1969 · The space race Success
stats: from Surveyor 3 (mission-era 535 ft; LROC positions imply ~155 m)
total time spacewalking on the surface

facts.label: Crew
facts.value: Charles "Pete" Conrad Jr. (commander), Richard F. Gordon Jr. (command module pilot, stayed in orbit), Alan L. Bean (lunar module pilot)

facts.label: Launch
facts.value: 14 Nov 1969, 11:22:00 a.m. EST (16:22:00 UTC), Kennedy Space Center LC-39A

facts.label: Lightning discharges
facts.value: Vehicle-triggered electrical discharges at T+36.5 s and T+52 s; John Aaron's "SCE to Auxiliary" call, executed by Bean, restored telemetry

facts.label: Lunar touchdown
facts.value: 19 Nov 1969, 06:54:35 UTC (GET 110:32:36), Ocean of Storms (Oceanus Procellarum)

facts.label: Distance from Surveyor 3
facts.value: About 160 m (535 ft) by the mission-era NASA figure; NASA sources quote 535 to 600 ft, and modern LROC positions put the separation at roughly 155 m (LROC's site pages say about 170 yards, and the LROC coordinate table implies 156.8 m)

facts.label: Surface EVAs
facts.value: Two moonwalks: EVA-1 about 3 h 56 min, EVA-2 about 3 h 49 min, total roughly 7 h 45 min

facts.label: Surface stay
facts.value: About 31.5 hours on the Moon (touchdown 19 Nov 06:54 UTC to liftoff 20 Nov 14:25 UTC)

facts.label: Samples returned
facts.value: About 34.4 kg (75.7 lb) of rock and soil

facts.label: Surveyor 3 parts retrieved
facts.value: TV camera, sample scoop, and cabling cut off and brought back to study micrometeorite and radiation effects after 31 months on the Moon

facts.label: Splashdown
facts.value: 24 Nov 1969, 20:58:24 UTC (3:58:24 p.m. EST), South Pacific; recovered by USS Hornet

timeline: Launch from Kennedy Space Center, 16:22 UTC
Two electrical discharges strike the Saturn V (T+36.5 s, T+52 s)
Intrepid lands in the Ocean of Storms, about 160 m from Surveyor 3, 06:54:35 UTC
First EVA, color TV camera destroyed when aimed at the Sun
Second EVA, crew walks to Surveyor 3 and cuts off its camera
Intrepid lifts off from the Moon, 14:25:47 UTC
Splashdown in the South Pacific, recovered by USS Hornet, 20:58 UTC
